doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

title: Leaving New York for Potsdam
summary: Left for safety and family reasons, moving to a small town.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well that’s good to hear. Eventually you decided to get out of the New York scene. Was it New York or was it the music scene, really, or was it a combination?

A combination. My daughter was eight going towards nine at the time, and I said, “Krissy keeps complaining that she has to yell up at me where we live to come down and get her” because it wasn’t safe I guess. Well I was a typical Lebanese father. I’m very protective of my children, or my child. I said, “Enough of this, we have to take a cab to go to Brooklyn to go to the dentist, we have to take a cab uptown and I don’t want to get in the subway. It’s time we went to a small town. So I went to Potsdam. Not to put New York down, New York is still the greatest city in the world. It’s not the same today. If it were possible, but every time a band came to Potsdam or to Syracuse or Watertown or any place near us, and Shorty and I would go to hear the band, she’d say, “I expect you to get on the bus to go off with the band.” It was usually the Basie Band, and the guys would say, “Shiner, you’re late, get on the bus.” She says, “I wouldn’t be surprised if you got on the bus.
